q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
Let me analyze this question carefully.

## Analysis Framework

**(a) Time left until resolution:**
Today is 2026-08-22. Q2 FY2027 earnings would be released roughly in August 2026 when Q2 FY2027 results are announced. Based on standard earnings cycles, the forward guidance for Q3 FY2027 would likely be provided during the Q2 FY2027 earnings release in late August 2026. This means we're essentially at the current moment or very close to it - resolution is imminent (days away, not weeks/months).

**(b) Most likely outcome and why:**

The CURRENT RESEARCH provides extremely specific and actionable information: NVIDIA has **already released forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 on May 20, 2026, of $91.0 billion ± 2%**, which translates to a range of **$89.18 billion to $92.82 billion**.

The research also indicates:
- Wall Street analysts' average estimate is ~$91.9 billion (within the guided range)
- This assumes zero Data Center compute revenue from China
- Year-over-year revenue is expected to double vs. $46.7B in the year-ago quarter

The question asks specifically for "NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release (Revenue)." This guidance has already been disclosed at $91.0 billion ± 2%.

The most likely outcome is that the actual reported guidance remains at or very close to $91.0 billion, given that:
1. It was officially communicated by the company
2. Wall Street consensus ($91.9B) sits comfortably within the ± 2% range
3. There are only days until resolution, leaving minimal time for material changes in guidance
4. NVIDIA rarely revises guidance downward mid-quarter unless there are dramatic shifts

**(c) What would push the value lower?**
- Unexpected China-related geopolitical deterioration reducing demand
- AI market demand weakening unexpectedly
- Competitor announcements affecting NVIDIA's positioning
- Supply chain disruptions
- Macro deterioration affecting customer capex

**(d) What would push the value higher?**
- Better-than-expected demand for current generation GPUs
- Positive surprise announcements regarding China restrictions being lifted/eased
- Enterprise/cloud customers accelerating capex
- New product announcements driving demand
- Margin expansion opportunities

**(e) Base rate or historical reference values:**

The research provides a direct precedent: NVIDIA's May 20, 2026 Q2 FY2027 guidance was $91.0 billion ± 2%. This is not a historical average but rather the actual current guidance that the question is asking about.

## Probability Distribution Reasoning

Given that:
- The guidance range is $89.18B to $92.82B (the ± 2% from $91.0B)
- The question's numerical range is 99.5B to 115.5B (with open bounds)
- We're essentially at the moment of or immediately after the guidance release
- Wall Street consensus is $91.9B

The most likely outcome is that final guidance lands squarely in the $89-93B range, centered around $91.0B. There is very little time for meaningful changes.

The probability mass should be heavily concentrated around $91.0 billion, with gradual tails extending to either side based on the ± 2% tolerance and potential for modest surprises.

**Distribution:**
- 10th percentile (lower tail): ~$89.5 billion - represents below-guidance scenarios
- 50th percentile (median): ~$91.0 billion - the stated guidance point
- 90th percentile (upper tail): ~$92.5 billion - represents modest upside surprises

NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, released on May 20, 2026, predicts $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027/). This guidance explicitly assumes no Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027/).

Wall Street analysts' average estimate for Q2 FY2027 revenue is around $91.9 billion, placing it within NVIDIA's guided range [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). This implies a year-over-year revenue doubling, compared to $46.7 billion in the year-ago quarter [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). Gross margins are expected to be 74.9% (GAAP) and 75.0% (non-GAAP), plus or minus 50 basis points [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm).
